regimes.name: Sole trader (ABN holder)
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals carrying on business under an ABN; taxed as resident individuals on net business income

socialContributions.name: Medicare levy
socialContributions.base: Taxable income (reduced or nil below low-income thresholds, which vary by year and were not verified)

regimes.reserveBasis: At AUD 108,352 (ABS average weekly ordinary time earnings AUD 2,083.70 x 52, May 2026): income tax 23,026 + Medicare levy 2,167 = 25,193, i.e. 23.3% of gross; assumes no deductible expenses, no LITO.

deadlines.name: Individual income tax return (income year ends 30 June)
PAYG instalments (quarterly, for those on the instalment system; 28 Oct, 28 Feb, 28 Apr, 28 Jul)

regimes.notes: Income year 1 Jul 2026 - 30 Jun 2027 (2026/27): 15% rate on 18,201-45,000 confirmed by secondary sources (cut from 16% on 1 Jul 2026, legislated further cut to 14% from 1 Jul 2027); 0% tax-free threshold of AUD 18,200 is modelled as the first bracket, so allowanceMinor is 0 to avoid double counting. Medicare levy 2% (PwC); low-income reduction thresholds and Medicare levy surcharge ignored; LITO ignored. GST 10% (PwC), registration at GST turnover of AUD 75,000 (ATO guidance as summarised by search; ATO site blocked). No compulsory social security; superannuation is voluntary for sole traders (PwC: concessional cap AUD 32,500 for 2026/27). Return due 31 Oct, later when lodged via a registered tax agent. PAYG instalment dates per PwC; the ATO site was unreachable (HTTP 403) so ATO pages were not read directly.

regimes.name: Sole trader / self-employed
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals earning self-employment income, taxed as residents on net profit

socialContributions.name: ACC Earners' Levy (non-work injury cover), self-employed
ACC Work Levy (average across classification units; actual rate depends on industry)
socialContributions.base: Liable earnings, capped at the maximum liable earnings

socialContributions.name: ACC Working Safer Levy
socialContributions.base: Liable earnings, capped at the maximum liable earnings

regimes.reserveBasis: At NZD 90,000 (about NZD 1,730 average weekly earnings x 52): income tax 19,578 + ACC levies (1.75%+0.69%+0.08%) 2,268 = 21,846, i.e. 24.3% of gross; assumes no deductible expenses.

deadlines.name: Income tax return IR3 (tax year ends 31 March)
Provisional tax instalments, standard option (28 Aug, 15 Jan, 7 May); GST-registered 6-monthly filers pay 2 instalments (28 Oct, 7 May)

regimes.notes: NZ tax year 1 Apr - 31 Mar; the 2026/27 year starts 1 Apr 2026. Brackets in force since 31 Jul 2024 per PwC, which states thresholds were last modified in 2024; no 2026/27 change found but not confirmed on the IRD site (IRD pages returned 404 or were unreachable). Instalment days vary (28 Aug, 15 Jan, 7 May); the quarterly entry uses day 28 with months [8,1,5] as a compact encoding, actual days are 28 Aug, 15 Jan, 7 May. ACC 2026/27 figures (earners levy 1.75/100, maximum liable earnings NZD 156,641, minimum NZD 50,501, work levy average 0.69/100, working safer 0.08/100) come from third-party summaries of the ACC/Gazette levy notice, not read from acc.co.nz; levy applies on liable earnings, minimum earnings rule modelled as floor. GST 15% (PwC); registration threshold NZD 60,000 over 12 months per third-party guides (IRD page not read). Tax agent extension to 31 March for the return (PwC). KiwiSaver is voluntary for the self-employed. Terminal tax date not verified.

regimes.name: Individual business operator (Ge Ti Gong Shang Hu)
regimes.appliesTo: Registered individually-owned business households taxed on business operating income
regimes.reserveBasis: At CNY 124,110 net business income: taxable 64,110 after the CNY 60,000 deduction, tax per 5-35% brackets halved by the 50% reduction for annual taxable income up to CNY 2m (to end-2027) = 2,456, i.e. 2.0%; social insurance not included (unverified).

deadlines.name: IIT business income: quarterly prepayment (15 days after quarter end: 15 Apr, 15 Jul, 15 Oct, 15 Jan)
IIT business income: annual return (secondary source)

regimes.notes: Brackets (5-35%) per PwC; CNY 60,000 annual deduction per PwC (claimable against either comprehensive or business income, not both). 50% reduction of IIT on annual taxable income up to CNY 2 million for individually-owned businesses runs 1 Jan 2023 to 31 Dec 2027 (secondary sources, not read from STA). VAT: small-scale taxpayers pay 1% in 2026-2027 (normally 3%) with exemption if quarterly sales are below CNY 300,000 (monthly below CNY 100,000) per PwC; general taxpayers 13/9/6%; the registration threshold field holds the quarterly exemption limit, the formal general-taxpayer threshold (CNY 5m annual) was not verified. Self-employed social insurance (flexible-employment pension/medical) is set by city and was not verified, so socialContributions is empty. 2026 rates confirmed unchanged by PwC (page reviewed 2026). Average wage used is not source-verified.

regimes.name: Freelancer comprehensive income (labour remuneration)
regimes.appliesTo: Resident individuals receiving labour remuneration without an employer; comprehensive income rules

incomeTax.base: Annual taxable comprehensive income after standard deduction

regimes.reserveBasis: At CNY 124,110 receipts: 80% taxable = 99,288, less CNY 60,000 deduction = 39,288; tax per 3-45% brackets = 1,409, i.e. 1.1%; social insurance and special additional deductions not included.

deadlines.name: Annual IIT reconciliation (1 Mar - 30 Jun of following year)

regimes.notes: Labour remuneration (services without employer): 20% deduction so 80% taxable, per PwC; withholding by payer by the 15th of the following month. Annual reconciliation window 1 Mar - 30 Jun per PwC. Brackets per PwC (marginal rates; quick-deduction amounts omitted, which are only a calculation shortcut). Special additional deductions (child education etc.) not applied. Small-scale VAT 1% (2026-2027) with CNY 300,000 quarterly exemption applies to freelancers who issue invoices.

regimes.name: Sole proprietorship profits tax (unincorporated business)
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals carrying on a trade, profession or business in Hong Kong with Hong Kong-sourced profits; assessed on profits (basis period, usually 12 months to 31 Dec or 31 Mar)

incomeTax.base: Assessable profits (two-tiered rates: 7.5% on first HKD 2m, 15% above; only one entity per person may use the lower tier)

socialContributions.name: MPF mandatory contribution, self-employed person
socialContributions.base: Relevant income; none below HKD 85,200 per year, base capped at HKD 360,000 per year (maximum contribution HKD 18,000)

regimes.reserveBasis: At HKD 267,600 profits (median monthly earnings HKD 22,300 x 12): profits tax 7.5% = 20,070 + MPF 5% = 13,380 = 33,450, i.e. 12.5%; no allowances applied under profits tax (personal assessment may lower this).

deadlines.name: Tax return - Individuals (BIR60) with business income: issued first working day of May, due 3 months after issue (approximate date; exact date printed on the return)
Provisional + final tax payable in two instalments (dates on the assessment notice)

regimes.notes: Profits tax rates 7.5%/15% for unincorporated businesses per IRD guidance as summarised by search (IRD pam56e, gov.hk), PwC page did not give them; 2026/27 rates not separately confirmed. No VAT/GST in Hong Kong (PwC). MPF self-employed: 5% of relevant income, minimum HKD 7,100/month (85,200/yr), maximum HKD 30,000/month (360,000/yr) per MPFA; contributions deductible up to HKD 18,000. Instalment months (January and April) per PwC; day not stated. Median earnings is a proxy for the national average and is from Q2 2025.

regimes.name: Sole proprietor under personal assessment / salaries-tax-style bands
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals with Hong Kong-sourced business profit electing personal assessment; progressive bands capped by the standard rate

incomeTax.base: Net assessable income after deductions and allowances

socialContributions.name: MPF mandatory contribution, self-employed person
socialContributions.base: Relevant income; none below HKD 85,200 per year, base capped at HKD 360,000 per year (maximum contribution HKD 18,000)

regimes.reserveBasis: At HKD 267,600: net after MPF deduction 254,220, less HKD 145,000 basic allowance = 109,220; tax per 2-17% bands = 4,922 + MPF 13,380 = 18,302, i.e. 6.8%.

deadlines.name: Tax return - Individuals (BIR60) with business income: issued first working day of May, due 3 months after issue (approximate date; exact date printed on the return)
Provisional + final tax payable in two instalments (dates on the assessment notice)

regimes.notes: Personal assessment (elective; lets personal allowances offset business profits, tax is the lower of assessed on profits tax or personal assessment). Bands 2/6/10/14/17% of HKD 50,000 each and the 15%/16% standard rate cap (first HKD 5m / remainder) per PwC for 2025/26; 2026/27 bands not separately confirmed. 2026/27 allowances per PwC: basic HKD 145,000, married HKD 290,000, child HKD 140,000/280,000, dependent parent HKD 55,000-110,000; allowanceMinor holds the single basic allowance. MPF contribution deductible up to HKD 18,000. The standard rate cap is not modelled in the brackets.

regimes.name: Individual under new tax regime (default)
regimes.appliesTo: Resident individuals/proprietors on net business income, default regime without most deductions
regimes.reserveBasis: Illustrative INR 1,500,000 net profit (no official national average wage verified; below INR 12 lakh the 87A rebate makes tax nil): tax per slabs x 1.04 cess = 109,200, i.e. 7.3%; GST collected is pass-through and excluded.

deadlines.name: Advance tax instalments (15% / 45% / 75% / 100% cumulative)
Income tax return, business/profession not requiring audit (PwC; statute date was 31 July - see notes)

regimes.notes: Slabs and 87A rebate (INR 60,000 where income up to INR 12 lakh) per PwC for FY 2025/26 and subsequent years; no FY 2026/27 change found, Income-tax Act 2025 takes effect 1 Apr 2026 with unchanged rates (not verified on incometax.gov.in). 4% cess on tax; surcharge above INR 50 lakh ignored. Basic exemption is the 0% slab so allowanceMinor is 0. No mandatory social security for the self-employed (EPF covers employees only per PwC). GST 18% general rate (PwC); registration threshold INR 20 lakh for services (INR 10 lakh in special-category states) and INR 40 lakh for goods is from general knowledge and not source-verified in this pass. Advance tax needed if liability exceeds INR 10,000; presumptive 44ADA/44AD taxpayers pay a single instalment by 15 March (not verified). PwC lists 31 Aug for non-audit business cases and 31 Oct for audit cases (audit if turnover above INR 10m or professional receipts above INR 5m).

regimes.name: Individual under old tax regime
regimes.appliesTo: Resident individuals opting for the old regime with deductions
regimes.reserveBasis: Illustrative INR 1,500,000 net profit less INR 150,000 Section 80C-type deduction = 1,350,000; tax per old-regime slabs x 1.04 cess = 226,200, i.e. 15.1%.

deadlines.name: Advance tax instalments (15% / 45% / 75% / 100% cumulative)
Income tax return, business/profession not requiring audit (PwC; statute date was 31 July - see notes)

regimes.notes: Old regime slabs per PwC (higher exemption for age 60+ ignored); 87A rebate only up to INR 5 lakh income. Deductions available: up to INR 150,000 for eligible investments (80C-type) and a further INR 50,000 for notified pension scheme per PwC. Same GST, advance tax and filing rules as the new regime.

regimes.name: Sole proprietor (Kojin Jigyonushi), blue or white return
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals with business or freelance income filing a Kakutei Shinkoku

incomeTax.base: Taxable income after deductions (national income tax; 2.1% surtax and 10% resident tax extra)

socialContributions.name: National Pension (Kokumin Nenkin), Category 1 insured, flat premium FY2026 (JPY 17,920 per month)
National Health Insurance (Kokumin Kenko Hoken) income-based part, Tokyo 23 wards FY2026: medical 7.51% + support 2.80% + child support 0.27%
socialContributions.base: Previous-year income minus JPY 430,000 basic deduction; rates differ by municipality

socialContributions.name: National Health Insurance per-capita levy (Tokyo 23 wards FY2026: 47,600 + 17,600 + 1,873), per insured person

regimes.reserveBasis: At JPY 4,870,000 (NTA 2025 average private-sector pay) treated as freelance revenue with no expenses: blue-return deduction 650,000; National Pension 215,040; NHI 468,055; national tax 155,387 (incl. 2.1% surtax) after basic deduction 1,040,000; resident tax 315,690; enterprise tax 66,000 (5%, only specified trades); total 1,220,172 = 25.1%.

deadlines.name: Final income tax return (kakutei shinkoku), filing window mid-Feb to 15 Mar (next business day if weekend)
Consumption tax return for sole proprietors (statutory date, not in PwC)
Preliminary national tax payment, 1st instalment (yotei nozei), if previous-year tax after withholding was JPY 150,000 or more
Preliminary national tax payment, 2nd instalment
Resident tax instalments (June, August, October, January; exact day per municipality)

regimes.notes: JPY has no minor unit: all amounts and brackets in this object are whole yen, not yen x 100. National brackets per PwC (5-45%), plus 2.1% reconstruction surtax; resident tax 10% (4% prefectural + 6% municipal) plus JPY 5,000 per capita (not source-verified); resident basic deduction stays JPY 430,000. 2026 reform (Diet approval 31 Mar 2026): national basic deduction for total income up to JPY 1.32m-4.89m is JPY 1,040,000 for 2026 and 2027 (permanent JPY 620,000 plus temporary special addition); JPY 670,000 for income to 6.55m, JPY 620,000 for 6.55m-23.5m (PwC). allowanceMinor uses 1,040,000. Blue-return special deduction JPY 650,000 (double-entry plus e-Tax), 550,000 paper, 100,000 simplified books (secondary sources; the 2026 reform changes apply from tax year 2027). National Pension JPY 17,920/month for FY2026 (Japan Pension Service). NHI figures are Tokyo 23-ward FY2026 rates (Ota ward page via search); annual caps for medical+support+child support 670,000+260,000+30,000 = 960,000 (excl. long-term care 170,000 for ages 40-64); other municipalities differ. Consumption tax 10% (reduced 8% for food ignored); exempt if taxable sales in the base period (two years earlier) are JPY 10m or less (NTA); invoice-system registration voluntary for small businesses, the 20% special measure window ended 30 Sep 2026. Enterprise tax 5% with JPY 2.9m deduction applies only to specified trades and was not source-verified.

regimes.name: Sole proprietor (Gaein Sauppja)
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals with business income filing comprehensive income tax in May

incomeTax.base: Net business income after deductions (local income tax of 10% of this tax is extra)

socialContributions.name: National Pension (regional subscriber, pays full 9.5% in 2026)
socialContributions.base: Declared monthly income; upper limit KRW 6,590,000 per month from July 2026 (annual base cap shown); lower limit not verified (KRW 400,000 per month in the prior year)

socialContributions.name: National Health Insurance (regional subscriber, income-based part; 2026 rate 7.19%, property/vehicle points and long-term care surcharge not modelled)

regimes.reserveBasis: At KRW 50,460,000 (about KRW 4.205m per month x 12, secondary source): pension 9.5% = 4,793,700 (deductible), NHI 7.19% = 3,628,074, taxable 44,166,300 after KRW 1.5m deduction, tax per brackets + 10% local = 5,901,440; total 14,323,214 = 28.4%; assumes no expenses and likely overstates NHI.

deadlines.name: Comprehensive income tax return and payment (1-31 May; next business day if weekend)
Interim prepayment of comprehensive income tax (half of previous year's tax, notified by tax office)
VAT final return, simplified taxpayers (annual) and second-half general taxpayers
VAT first-half return for general taxpayers; prepayment notice payment for simplified taxpayers

regimes.notes: KRW has no minor unit: all amounts and brackets are whole won, not won x 100. Brackets 6-45% per PwC (income from 1 Jan 2023), plus local income tax of 10% of the tax; no 2026 bracket change found in PwC. Basic deduction KRW 1.5m per person (PwC); pension contributions fully deductible; business-income taxpayers get no flat standard deduction. National Pension: 9.5% in 2026 rising 0.5 point a year to 13% in 2033 (news coverage; PwC shows 4.75% employee + 4.75% employer); income cap KRW 6.59m per month from July 2026 (PwC, Herald). NHI rate 7.19% (2026 and frozen for 2027, news); regional NHI actually combines income, property and vehicle points and adds long-term care, so the modelled rate is approximate. VAT 10%; every business must register, simplified taxpayer status (KRW 104m annual supply threshold since July 2024) is from general knowledge, not source-verified. Deadlines for return, 30 Nov interim payment and VAT dates from PwC plus secondary tax-calendar sources; complex filers (sincere-reporting confirmation) get 30 June.

regimes.name: Sole proprietor / self-employed
regimes.appliesTo: Resident individuals with trade or business income

incomeTax.base: Chargeable income after reliefs and deductions

socialContributions.name: MediSave contribution, self-employed (SEP), age 35 to under 45 band
socialContributions.base: Annual net trade income; due only if NTI above SGD 6,000; rates phase in up to SGD 18,000 and vary by age (8% under 35, 9% age 35-45, 10% age 45-50, 10.5% from 50 per third-party summaries); capped at the age-band maximum and the MediSave contribution ceiling

regimes.reserveBasis: At SGD 69,300 net trade income (median gross monthly income 5,775 x 12, includes employer CPF): MediSave 9% = 6,237 (fully deductible); chargeable income 62,063 after SGD 1,000 earned income relief; tax per YA2026 brackets = 2,094; total 8,331 = 12.0%.

deadlines.name: Income tax return (e-Filing deadline, Form B for self-employed)
Tax payable within one month of the Notice of Assessment (GIRO instalments available)

regimes.notes: Brackets for YA2026 (income earned in 2025) per PwC; YA2027 (income earned in 2026) brackets not verified. Resident rates start with a 0% band to SGD 20,000. Earned income relief SGD 1,000 under age 55 (PwC); other reliefs not applied; total relief cap SGD 80,000. YA2026 rebates not verified. MediSave: official CPF structure confirmed (age and NTI based, only if NTI above SGD 6,000) but the 2026 rate table could not be read; 9% for age 35-45 matches an IRAS worked example. Self-employed make no CPF Ordinary or Special Account contributions (voluntary only). Compulsory MediSave is billed after the Notice of Assessment. GST 9% (PwC); mandatory registration if taxable turnover exceeds SGD 1 million in a calendar year or is expected to in the next 12 months (IRAS, via search). Filing date 18 April per PwC; the payment deadline entry month 6 is approximate because NOAs are issued from about June and tax is due one month later.

regimes.name: Sole proprietor / freelancer
regimes.appliesTo: Residents with business or professional income

incomeTax.base: Net taxable income after exemptions and deductions

socialContributions.name: NHI supplementary premium on professional practice income (code 9A), withheld by payer
socialContributions.base: Each single payment of professional practice income of TWD 20,000 or more

regimes.reserveBasis: At TWD 760,632 (DGBAS 2025 average total annual earnings) as net professional income: taxable 532,632 after TWD 97,000 exemption and TWD 131,000 standard deduction; tax at 5% = 26,632; NHI supplementary premium 2.11% = 16,049; total 42,681 = 5.6%; regular NHI premium and labour insurance for the self-employed not included (unverified).

deadlines.name: Annual individual income tax return (1-31 May, no extension)
Provisional tax for sole proprietorship business income (1-30 Sep; not source-verified)

regimes.notes: TWD amounts stored x 100 like other currencies with cents. Brackets (5/12/20/30/40%, first band to TWD 590,000) are for the 2025 return filed in 2026 per PwC; a media report of CPI-indexed amounts for 2026 income (exemption 101,000, standard deduction 136,000, first band 610,000) could not be verified against an official announcement, so 2026 income-year rules are not confirmed. Exemption TWD 97,000 plus single standard deduction TWD 131,000 (PwC) combined in allowanceMinor; basic living expense differential TWD 213,000 per person not applied; separate 20% basic income tax above TWD 7.5m. Business tax (VAT) standard 5%; since 1 Jan 2025 monthly-sales exemption thresholds are TWD 100,000 (goods) and TWD 50,000 (services) per KPMG/Orbitax via search, small-scale businesses under TWD 200,000 per month may pay a fixed 1% on assessed sales; registrationThresholdMinor holds the services threshold of TWD 50,000. NHI supplementary premium 2.11% per NHI administration table via search. Cost-deduction ratios for professional practice income by occupation not verified.
